articleTitle: A Fibre Optic Link for EMP Measurements
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Fibre-optic cable are very attractive in performing EMP Measurements because of the nonconducting nature of the cable. They do not form ground loops and do not pick up or radiate electric signals. They carry the measured responses of the system under test as light signals out of the EMP simulator. A system is described consisting of a transmitter, a fibre-optic cable and a receiver. In the transmitter a light emitting diode is amplitude modulated by the applied electric signal. The emitted light signal is carried via a glass-fibre cable to a remotely located receiver, In the receiver the light signal is converted Into the original electric signal by an avalanche photo detector. The Analog system has a bandwidth from 250 Hz to 250 MHz and a dynamic range of +45 dB and -35 dB. The cable has a length of 40 m. The transmitter is constructed in such a way that it can serve as a part of the ground plane of a B-sensor.

articleTitle: A Swiss View of General Nemp Protection Principles
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper is a short representation of some general principles taken into account before locking into the design of real NEMP protection measures. In fact a procedure is described by which the very first stage of protecting a system against NEMP effects is defined.

articleTitle: EMI Performance of Bonneville Power Administration'S Prototype 1200 KV Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper presents the results of the first year's measurements on an 8 × 41 mm conductor bundle at the Bonneville Power Administrations 1200 kV Lyons Test Facility. Results of the first-year's testing at this facility is compared with EMI measurements conducted on a nearby 525 kV operating line. The results show the radio and television interference and audible noise for the 1200 kV 8 conductor bundle to be less than the 525 kV 2 conductor bundle. The paper also compares the 60 Hz electric fields near ground for the 1200 and 525 kV lines.

articleTitle: Towards A New Policy of Radio-Spectrum Utilization (before and after the WARC 1979)
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: An overall review of principal problems, concerning present and future policy of radio-spectrum utilization is given in the introduction to the paper. Then, such problems as: high-power, large coverage area - versus low-power, small coverage area systems, modern modulation systems; “on the air” - versus “ wired ” systems; the future of HF communications, frequencies for scientific research; spectrum pollution limitation; the sharing - versus bind subdivision principle; the “planning” - versus “ flexible” frequency assignment principle and finally spectrum efficiency criteria are discussed more in detail. The conclusions contain some thoughts which may be of use when discussing positions to be adopted for the WARC 1979.

articleTitle: Dipole's E.M. Field Attenuation Versus Distance in near Field and above Reflecting Ground
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: In this work, calculated attenuation values taking into account the far and near field components simultaneously are compared with the results of sperimentai measurements carried out in two test stations. A final table shows the measurements and calculi results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Frequency Synthesizers
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility of frequency synthesizers depends on the level of the omnipresent noise and discrete spurious signals. In the paper we discuss, in detail, the noise properties of individual building blocks (oscillators, frequency multipliers and dividers, mixers and phase detectors, buffer amplifiers, and phase lock loops) and investigate the noise characteristics of actual frequency synthesizers.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Electric Power Systems
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The recent enormous increase of thyristors presents new serious problone in relation between electric power systems end consonare of electrical energy. There are many cases where the distortion of the naine wave form by the operation of thyristor devices of one consumer cause the melfunctionning of the equipment of another consumer. The problem solved in the paper involves the determination of the interference due to the harmonics in power systems. Influence of the naine impedances and importance of the determination of the harmonics flow direction.

articleTitle: Experimental Procedure to Determine Limits of ISM Interference Affecting Navigational ILS Equipment.
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: To assess interference field limits required to protect a specified radio service it is necessary to proceed on an experimental statistical way to reach normally a compromise between the minimum acceptable protection for the worst conditions and the additional cost of the protecting device used. When the service has a vital importance, as an aeronautical aid, the protection should be such to guarantee for all cases a complete reliable operation, of the vital aid equipment, independent from any cost compromise.

articleTitle: Modeling and Measurements of Man-Made Noise
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The more important difference between a single man-made noise and a general interference environment is the decomposition of this environment in elementary interferences, that appear and disappear at random and independant moments. So, it is possible now to consider two manners for resolving the man-made noise modeling: a) It is possible to consider the physical processus as a queuing system, where the servers number is infinite, and the comparison between the real model and the theory of queues is that: 1) Interferences represent customers 2) The service time is the duration of interferences 3) The state of the queue is defined by the number of interferences that are simultaneous. b) The physical process is considered as a birth-death process, and the λ<inf>j</inf> and μ<inf>j</inf> numbers represent respectively infinitesimal transition probabilities that the j<sup>th</sup> noise occurs and vanishes. The more natural hypotheses are: <tex>$λj = λ$</tex> <tex>$μj = ju$</tex> We are now studying these models one after another.

articleTitle: On Limits of Radio Interference from Vehicles in the Frequency Range 30-1000 MHz
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper discusses some aspects of a question about limits of radio interference from vehicles, which are sufficient for protection of radio reception with a required high reliability. Information is given on new limits accepted in the USSR.

articleTitle: Land-Mobile Base Station Antenna Site Design Considerations
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper describes techniques used at common land-mobile base station sites to control interference between station antennas.

articleTitle: Common Features and Differences of EMC Problems Regarding Wire-Bound Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: As far as wire-bound communication systems are considered the control of EMC problems becomes more and more important.

articleTitle: The Simulation of Line Interference
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: In order to design reliable electronic equipment the imperfections in a industrial electric power system must be considered. The equipment must be so designed that it is immune to the types of defects that may expected. We speak of susceptibility and say that the equipment must not be "susceptible" to interference or faults or we can say that the equipment must be "immune" to them.

articleTitle: A Survey and Review of Recent Literature on Lightning and Lightning Protection
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: During the past few years research in the areas of lightning and lightning protection has taken on new emphasis. The major reason for this has been the growing application of sensitive solid state electronics in a variety of systems. This paper is a survey and review of the literature that is available on recent and on-going work being performed in the U.S. and some other countries. Subject areas covered are new developments in lightning phenomenology and effects, shielding bonding and grounding techniques, and protection devices, A bibliography of significant publications and a list of references is provided. Information sources and procedures for obtaining documents is also included.

articleTitle: Propagation Studies of Electromagnetic Waves through Plane Tissues
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: A study is being made to estimate the reflection coefficient, transmission coefficient, surface-charge density, and current density of a plane tissue, when exposed to electromagnetic energy. The tissue thickness is varied and the results are compared and discussed for different frequency ranges. Further the experimental results in the microwave region are also given.

articleTitle: Digital Measurement of Fast Transients on Power Supply Lines
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This contribution describes in some details an approach towards the measurement, storage and evaluation of fast transients on the power line. In order to make automatic computer evaluation of the measured data possible, a fast transient recorder was built, the central part of which is a fast, parallel analog-to-digital converter, followed by a simple data reduction circuit and a fast memory. The fast transient recorder was used for a large series of measurements in various industrial plants and near various sources of power line transients. The recorder waveforms were investigated with respect to their amplitude statistics, shape, and spectral behaviour.

articleTitle: Effective Suppression of Ignition Noise
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: A simplified equivalent circuit of the internal combustion engine ignition system and relations are given permitting the determination of impulsive noise currents in the succesive spark generation stages within the ignition system wiring. The possibility of utilizing the results of the simplified noise generation analysis within the VHP frequency range is discussed. Some techniques are indicated which at low costs may ensure considerable reduction of ignition noise.

articleTitle: EMP Coupling to Long Cables
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: An approximation is developed for the interaction of an arbitrary em pulse with an infinite cylinder. The theory is extended to finite cylinders and a detailed comparison is made with published results and experiments carried out at AWRE.

articleTitle: An Outline of the EMP Activity in Italy
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The study of the Nuclear Electromagnetic Pulse (IMP) is taking more and more importance in the electrical engineering of electronic equipment/system survivability in an EMP environment. In the development of new systems some years ago the EMP hardening requirement was considered desirable; now it has became essential. There is considerable lack of information outside the USA and in addition the available documentation is not easily accessible. In the effort of trying to fill up the gap in this specific field it seans necessary both to gain experience in the IMP hardening design and to develop testing techniques suitable to verify the EMP survivability characteristics of equipment and systems. The availability of a system which provides the excitation used for EMP simulation is deemed desirable. Within the frame of EMP studies a joint study team of Aeritalia and C.A.M.E.N. engineers has been established with the aim of performing an analysis of a proper simulation for experimental testing purposes. On the basis of the work developed by the study team this paper investigates the following points: - the definition of the EMP to be simulated and consequently the type of simulator - the pulsed power generation system - the data acquisition and processing

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Interference and Shielding Analysis
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Several years ago, in connection with the feasibility study for an electronic system application, it was determined that magnetic field interference inside a metal column was one of the key problems to be investigated. Precise magnetic field variation at specific areas within the column was restricted to a predetermined value for various design configurations so that functional accuracy of the system was not effected. Because the design configurations (geometry of the problem) are usually not amenable to a purely analytical calculation of the magnetic field distribution within the system, a combined analytical and numerical approach was taken to determine the field distribution. Shielding design formulae are needed in case the field variation is higher than desirable. The objective of this paper is to present some of the results obtained during the study.

articleTitle: Radio-Frequency Attenuating Connectors - Applications of Inductive Coupling
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Improvement in safety standards in respect of electrically initiated explosive devices, particularly in aircraft and missile systems, has become an increasing problem relative to the RF and NEMC environment. However, by the use of the inductive coupling it is practicable to introduce a new order of safety from RF and electrostatic hazards, both in the installed and hand-held situation, together with many other advantages relating to reliability and performance criteria. This paper considers the problems and conventional approach, then describes methods by which the increasingly stringent requirements can be met. It suggests some civil applications for the technique and includes illustrations of practical devices already achieved or under development.

articleTitle: Analysis of Transmission Systems Equipment Immunity to Impulsive Interference
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: On the basis of analysis of expressions for calculation of stability of transmission-systems equipment under influence of man-made interference the expedience of establishing the limits for different interference parameters is determined.

articleTitle: A Statistical Method of Assessment of the Effectiveness of Implementation of CISPR Limits and of Electromagnetic Environment State which is Due to Man-Made Interference
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Expressions are presented, which relate statistical characteristics of a signal, of interference, of mains decoupling factors and of external immunity of receiving installations to performance of radio systems in the presence of man-made Interference, The paper suggests formulas of assessment of effectiveness of interference suppression according to CISPR limits, of effectiveness of abatement of interferences along their propagation paths and of improvement of external immunity. The effectiveness of all these measures is expressed in a variation of a magnitude of a guaranteed signal. Examples are given of assessment of parameters of probability distributions of the magnitudes of interference made from sampling characteristics which are obtained when checking the compliance with limits. Examples of assessment of the above-mentioned measures are presented.

articleTitle: EMP-Induced Currents and Fields in Shelters
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The electromagnetic fields inside of shelters usually have different sources which roughly can be classified in three categories: fields which penetrate the shield, fields which pass through apertures, and fields which are associated with currents on cables and other conduits which penetrate the electromagnetic shielding. The designing principles how to achieve optimum balance between the different protective measures are known. In my talk I shall concentrate on the problems how to estimate fields of different origin in a structure which is already in operation and which was not systematically hardened against EMP.

articleTitle: EMC in Lightweight Helicopters Special Problems and Experience in Design and Control
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: In order to ensure the compatible operation of various units of electronic and electrical equipment within a system, all technical and economical possibilities must be exploited in the course of planning and development with the aim of verifying the appropriate EMC principles. The more compact and complex a system is, the more difficult is its design, mainly due to the importance of weight-saving and the lack of a closed shielding airframe.

articleTitle: Method of Moment Thin Wire Computer Program Comparison for Complex Structures and Coarse Accuracy
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Three typical thin-wire moment method computer programs OS (sinusoidal Galerkin) SYR (triangle Galerkin), and WRSMOM (pulse expansion-impulse weighting) are compared. They are applied to four antenna models — two simple and two complex. The complex models are representative of shipboard "twin fan" antennas. The primary purpose is to determine if a "best" computer program exists given "coarse" accuracy (within ∼3 dB of converged results) as acceptable in predicting the driving point impedances and farfield radiation patterns exhibited by such structures

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigations of Site Attenuation by Means of Mutual Impedance between Antennas
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: In this paper, theoretical values of site attenuation are presented. They were obtained by means of mutual impedance between antennas. Its theoretical analysis and calculation procedures are described. Some of calculated values are compared with measured ones and the results are discussed.

articleTitle: Broadcasting Antenna Models for EMI Prediction
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Mathematical models of broadcasting antennae with omnidirectional and shaped horizontal patterns are presented in the paper. The models are useful for EMI prediction and especially for computer simulation of broadcasting systems.

articleTitle: EMC and the WARC-79 Planning in the Fixed-Satellite Service
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The Fall of this year will see nearly all of the world's nations represented at the Geneva World Administrative Radio Conference (WARC'79) for the purpose of amending the International Radio Regulations. One of the most important tasks of that Conference will be to reach agreement on a new Table of Frequency Allocations and on the provisions by which the use of the new Table will be regulated.

articleTitle: The Performance of Synchronisation by Wideband-Add-On-Signals
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: A method is proposed to synchronize communication networks by wideband-addon-signals. The system described here uses a synchronisation signal which results from a multiplicative combination of n subsignals of relative prime lengths. In the receivers each subsignal is reconstructed with correct phase and can be used for synchronisation purpose.

articleTitle: Influence of Man-Made Noise on the Reception of Standard Frequency Transmissions at VLF
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper deals with the influence of man-made noise when receiving the transmissions of the normal-frequency-transmitter DCF 77. After the introduction to special data of DCF 77 and mentioning some applications of the time- and frequency-information spread over Western Europe impulsive noise by power lines and traction noise by tramway-lines are discussed. After mentioning jamming interference by other VLF-transmitters some advice how to design normal-frequency-receivers at the presence of electromagnetic noise will be given.

articleTitle: Conducted and Radiated Interference Measurements in Light Pressurized Water Reactor Nuclear Power Stations.
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Magnitude of EMI and RFI in nuclear power stations is not adequately documented. Consequently an electromagnetic noise measurement program has been undertaken in a representative power station (a 900 MW PWR unit) in order to collect in-plant measurements of the electromagnetic field and other sources of disturbances at various locations and times. The program was at first directed towards the determination of the quality of AC, battery-DC and uninterruptible-AC power. Voltage and frequency variations, noise content, the shape of spikes and the duration of dropouts were investigated. In addition some experiments to check the effect of portable radio transmitters and receivers on control equipment are reported. After completion of this program, it is aimed that data transmission systems designers will be given numerical guidelines for the amount of noise they must protect again.

articleTitle: How to Fight EMI Propagating over Cables Achieving EMC by Adopting the Appropriate Cable Type and Layout
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Interconnect wiring or cabling between components, modules, racks, cabinets or systems is prone to pick up electromagnetic interference (EMI). Basically, one has to distinguish between two general EMI coupling modes: - ambient EMI fields coupling into cables, wires - EMI being coupled from one cable to another.

articleTitle: Empirical Models for Probability Distributions of Short-Term Mean Environmental Man-Made Radio Noise Levels
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Four new statistical-distribution models of increasing complexity (simple Gaussian, Gaussian from Chi-square, composite Gaussian, and Chi-square) are presented which can be used to predict the exceedence probabilities for short-term (≈1 min.) mean values of environmental man-made radio noise available power levels for low-gain vertically polarized antennas located near ground. The models are useful in predicting the probability that the short-term signal-to-noise ratio for a given communication system equals or exceeds a value required for successful communications. These models for each of three environmental categories (business, residential, and rural) are based upon data in CCIR Report 258-3 for the frequency band 0.25-250 MHz. Model intercomparisons are made, and the predicted distributions are compared with two measured distributions. It is concluded that these models are most useful in the probability interval 0.1 to 0.9. Further checks against measured data are needed to determine the limits of their applicability in the U.S. and elsewhere.

articleTitle: Use of Metal_Bonded Composite Polymers for Improvement of Screening Efficiency for Field Measurement of Small Signals
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Electromagnetic Interference plays a critical role in determining the sensitivity and success of test and control operations in noisy environments. The available shielding in the detection systems often fail to be adequate and have to be improved/repaired on site. A rapid and economic solution may be found in such cases by an in-situ application of a metal screen with the help of cold-bond polymer materials. The author has been using cold-curing polymers, both rigid and flexible, which have versatile bonding ability to a large number of engineering materials. These materials, ranging electrically from semi conductor to good insulator, have proved to he useful in different types of in-situ shielding jobs. Some of the materials and techniques involved in the successful use of metal-bonded composite polymers for in-situ improvement of screening efficiency are discussed.

articleTitle: EMP Response Estimation in Shielded Cables
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Several numerical and analytical techniques for determining the EMP response in cables have been developed by many authors. The analytical procedure presented in this paper proves to be a simple approach for computing the internal currents and voltages in cables having one or two shields for the quasistationary case. The basic idea lies in the application of the calculus of residues to the inverse Laplace transformation. Computed results are given.

articleTitle: Damping of Resonances in RFI Filters with RC Members
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The resonances in the passband of the RPI filter can be suppressed by introducing an RC member in the parallel, capacitivé branch of the filter. The paper describes an analitycal way of calculating components of the elemental "L" section filter as it works under odd interface conditions O/∞. More complex, multiple "L" section filters can be designed using a digital computer, such that the paper describes principles of the computer program as well. At the end, theoretical results are verified experimentaly and the results of measuring are also given.

articleTitle: Selected Susceptibility Problems of the General Use Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The paper deals with the problem of susceptibility of the general use electronic devices /GUED/ to electromagnetic /EM/ fields. This problem is growing parallel to the rapid growth of the HF power applications. Nearby located radiation sources cause that many GUED have to work in an EM environment of relatively high field strength. The insufficient immunity of electronic devices to extern EM fields is the most frequent cause of interferences which do occur. Using typical methods of radio- and TV-receiver measurements as well as typical methods of standard EM field generation the susceptibility of several GUED has been measured. The measurements showed that the majority of the investigated GUED was not adapted to work in the conditions of Irradiation by exterior EM fields of several volts per metre. To stear dear of conflicts between services utilizing the radiation sources and the users of the GUED on this field in the future we ought undertake certain steps towards solving this problem today.

articleTitle: Computer Studies of Satellite Broadcasting Systems
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper gives a short description of a PL/I program that has been applied in studies of interference in Satellite broadcasting systems. The program has been utilized in production of maps which show the quality of satellite TV in Scandinavia. Some examples illustrate the influence of transmitting antenna-pointing errors. An attempt is made to evaluate the electromagnetic compatibility of broadcasting from space.

articleTitle: Analysis and Measurement of R.F.I. Generated by DC/DC Converters
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to determine the radio frequency interferences generated by the switching-mode DC - DC converters, particularly the electromagnetic field emissions. These interferences are characterized by a broadband harmonic spectrum which starts from about 20 kHz (fundamental frequency) to 20 or 30 MHz. This has lead the French Post and Telecommunication Administration to define RFI standards for the DC/DC converters.

articleTitle: Ignition RFI Suppressor Testing Methods: A Comparison
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Two methods, recommended by CISPR for measurement of the effectiveness of anti-interference resistors, spark-plugs, cables, etc. used for suppression of radio noise generated by vehicle engine ignition systems, are compared.

articleTitle: The Subjective Assessment of Radio Interference Produced by Data Processing Equipment on LF and MF Broadcast Reception
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: In the past major sources of radio interference to LF and MF broadcast reception hare been those which generate Interference of a broadband nature. An exception to this is the narrow-band interference generated by the line tine base of television receivers. These broadband and narrowband interferences require different protection ratios for the same grade of impairment to reception. Data Processing Equipment is now becoming common in the domestic situation and the radio interference it generates is narrowband. This paper describes subjective tests in which the protection ratios required for broadband Interference and interference generated by data processing equipment are determined by a panel of listene» assessing the degree of annoyance induced. The conclusion drawn is that the protection ratio required for interference from data processing equipment is 10dB greater than that for broadband interference.

articleTitle: EMC, Lightning Protection and EMP-Requirements: The Necessity of Coordination in these Fields
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: With respect to their electromagnetic properties modern electric and electronic systems are subject to increasingly higher requirements. A survey of this is given in Fig. 1.

articleTitle: A Novel Low-Pass Filter for Protecting Electro-Explosive Devices in RF Environments
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This presentation describes a simple and inexpensive filter which takes advantage of the skin effect on wires in a lattice network to produce a low-pass frequency response characteristic. The filter eliminates the problem of accidental ignition of electro-explosive devices in high intensity radio frequency environments.

articleTitle: Induced Effects of Lightning on an All Composite Aircraft
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Results are presented for lightning induced cable currents and voltages on typical cable runs inside an all composite aircraft. Both a direct stroke and a nearby stroke are considered. Results are also. given for the case in which the aircraft is coated with 6-mil aluminum flame spray. It is shown that, as expected, the direct stroke induces the largest voltages, but the effects of the nearby strike are not negligible.

articleTitle: System – EMC Tendencies of a Worldwide Standardization and Cooperation
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Modern integrated systems, aircraft, tanks, cars or ships are combining more and more highly sophisticated equipment in an extremely small space, creating an increasing number of EMI problems. The electromagnetic compatibility therefore becomes worldwide more and more important and requires, especially because of the extended sales market for all kinds of electronic goods, a better cooperation and standardization for the basic integration and qualification tests. This paper will touch some of the according tendencies on both the commercial and military side, using the authors own experiences with some typical examples.

articleTitle: Disturbances in directly earthed transmission power systems caused by geomagnetic storms
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Without apparent reason, relay trippings in the directly earthed Swedish’ primary transmission system have occurred twice during recent years, disconnecting sections of transmission lines and transformers. The cause has been traced to the geomagnetic storms which occurred concurrently. Disturbances caused by these storms have earlier been observed in telecommunication and railway signalling systems but these interference phenomena will not apply to the power transmission systems. This report describes briefly the origin of these storms and how they affect the operation of the high-tension transmission system in Sweden. Effects of magnetic storms on apparatus include in the directly earthed transmission system are analyzed. Magnetic saturation of power transformers by direct currents occurring in connection with geomagnetic storms is found to be a determining factor in the origin of currents which cause tripping of the protective relays.

articleTitle: Small Signal Rectification Effects in Linear Transistor Circuitry
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Low frequency bipolar and field effect transistor circuitry which is operated in an RF or microwave environment is often found to be susceptible to RFI.(1, 2) classic examples of this effect are interference in automotive electronic braking or fuel injection circuitry from a nearby high powered transmitter or perhaps in a heart pacemaker when the wearer gets too near to a defective microwave oven.

articleTitle: Comparison of Power Measured by the MDS Clamp and Electric Field of the Interference
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper discusses the correlation between the measured values, using the interference power measuring method with the MDS clamp specified in CISPR Publ.2, and the electric field measurement with a dipole antenna. The electric fields were measured for three cases concerning the disposition of the mains lead. The first was one which is specified in CISPR Pub1.2; the mains lead being wrapped around the reel. The second was the same as the MDS clamp method; the mains lead being stretched in a straight line about 5 meters long. The third was the same as the second one but the MDS clamp was put on the mains lead and the position of the clamp was moved to get the maximum reading of the field. By these measurements, the following results were obtained. (1) When the mains lead was wrapped around the reel as specified in CISPR Publ.2, radiation was very weak in comparison with the calculated value by the equation <tex>$\mathrm{E}=7\sqrt{\mathrm{p}}/\mathrm{d}$</tex> (P: power, E: electric field, d:measuring distance). (2) The measured maximum electric field of interderence was less than the calculated value by about 10 dB or more.

articleTitle: Immunity Characteristics of Electronic Equipment and its Measurement
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Interference or (man-made) noise can penetrate into electronic equipment by means of electromagnetic radiation fields or by conducted voltages and currents. The latter are conducted to the equipment by connected cables (input, output, mains or auxiliary cables) and are often induced by ambient radiation fields.

articleTitle: “Emission Control Technology for Multinational Switching Power Systems”
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: In recent years, there has been a very rapid shift from linear to switching power systems. The current rate of switching technology growth is about 35% per year of the total power supply market.<sup>1</sup> Furthermore, the total power supply growth is about 500 million dollars per year or 20% per year, clearly a very large market.<sup>2</sup> It has been estimated that by 1985, over 50% of the total power systems will be a switching type. The main reasons for the rapid conversion to switching power supplies are: efficiency, lower operating temperatures, lighter and smaller size. Switching supplies have greater dynamic regulation range than linear or ferroresonant types. A considerable amount of progress has been made recently in development of new components which have resulted in very cost effective and reliable supplies, e.g., large scale integrated switching regulator control chips have been combined with the new generation of power transistors.

articleTitle: Estimation of Induced Fields and Power Absorption for Human Heads using an Ellipsoidal Model When Exposed to Electromagnetic Energy
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The perturbation technique is applied to find internal electric field to first-order approximation for ellipsoidal models that simulate human adult and infant heads in the presence of electromagnetic plane wave radiation. Calculations of time-averaged specific absorbed power and space-averaged specific absorbed power are given for six different orientations of the ellipsoid model with respect to the incident plane wave field vectors.

articleTitle: Using the Integrated Circuit Electromagnetic Susceptibility Handbook to Assess the Susceptibility of Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The McDonnell Douglas Astronautics Company (MDAC), under contract to the U. S. Naval Surface Weapons Center - Dahlgren Laboratory, has developed a technology base on integrated circuit electromagnetic susceptibility for use in precluding EMI in electronic systems. Two previous drafts issued on 4 June 1976 and 3 June 1977 were widely reviewed, and suggestions and comments received from these versions were incorporated into the final version.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Enclosures Behaviour. Comparison Data Analysis. -Part I.
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: A synthetic analysis of reverberating rooms behaviour and applications is carried out. Large reference to work done by authors and by other people is made, in order to give a complete outline of the problem. Data referring to various realizations are compared.

articleTitle: Propagation Medium of Radio Interference: Mathematical Model, Measurement of Characteristics, Establishing the Limits for Parameters
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The paper considers questions of construction of a mathematical model of a radio interference propagation medium, of measurement of parameters of this model and of establishing limits for characteristics of a propagation medium.

articleTitle: Current Status of RFI Predictions in Electronic Systems Containing Semiconductor Devices
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: It is widely recognized that electronic systems which are not specifically designed to operate at radio- and microwave frequencies can and sometimes do respond at those frequencies. The prevention of undesirable RF-induced responses imposes the requirements of: (1) predicting RFI effects in electronic systems, and (2) taking appropriate measures in the design of such systems to mitigate these effects. This paper is an overview of some of the basic approaches currently being pursued to predict RFI effects in electronic systems containing semiconductor discrete and integrated circuit devices. In theory, any nonlinear device can exhibit a spurious response to RF or microwave energy. However, some semiconductor devices are particularly sensitive because of their small size, high speed, and low operating signal levels. Moreover, trends to smaller, faster devices with lower signal levels, and the proliferation of RF sources should dictate that more attention be given to this area.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective and Nonlinear Characteristics of Low-Frequency EM Sensory Effects
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: It 1s known that pulsed electromagnetic waves are more effective than continuous waves in producing sensory effects 1n biological subjects. This implies that nonlinear mechanisms are an important contri buter to EM bioeffects. Auditory and visual (phosphene) sensations generated in human subjects through direct stimulation by low-frequency electric currents were studied to help characterize such mechanisms. Both sensory modalities displayed stimulus input-sensation output characteristics which were very frequency selective, exhibited adaption, and displayed nonlinearities. Sensory sensations were induced by current densities as low as 1 μΑ/cm<sup>2</sup>. The minimum thresholds of current for the phosphene and auditory effects occur, respectively, at 18 to 22 Hz and 60 to 90 Hz. The frequency cutoffs for the two effects were about 80 Hz and 200 Hz respectively for sinewave stimulations, however, a stimulus consisting of two sinewaves or a pulsed sinusoid extended the cutoff to higher carrier frequencies. It is known that a nerve membrane has a rectifying characteristic and a frequency dependent square law half-wave rectifier type model appears to satisfy the dual frequency data. Intermodulation data for both 2nd and 3rd order nonlinearities show a linear dependence on stimulus amplitude. Simple nonlinearities do not explain the pulsed sinusoid results.

articleTitle: Screening Characteristics of VHF Television Broadcasting Waves by Steel Towers of Overhead Power Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Television broadcasting waves are scattered by the construction of large power transmission lines, causing ghost images and screening interference to be sometimes generated at receiving points. This paper deals with the result of measurements to elucidate the screening characteristics of steel towers in power transmission lines with respect to television waves in the VHF band. The measurements were performed by radiating radio waves in the SHF band, which is 40 times higher in frequency than the VHF band, to five kinds of 1/40 scale model tower. The results can be summarized as follows: The difference between maximum and minimum screening loss levels obtained by rotating the model tower was approximately 3 to 5 dB when the distance between receiving point and model tower (R) was 1 to 4m, but the level difference was reduced to within 1 dB when the distance R reached 3 to 4 times ground distance equivalent to the tower height. For distances longer than 6m, the model tower was found to be replaceable with a finite cylindrical conductor having equivalent screening loss. Measured values of screening loss were in approximate agreement with the calculated values.

articleTitle: Nemp Simulation and Tests in Switzerland
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper reviews the Swiss activities on EMP testing and simulation without going into too many details. A description of the recently erected facility for EMP field generation is given as well as of the different available pulse generators to drive the field antennae and for direct injection. The equipment for testing cables and protective circuits is presented and the measurement arrangements for CW- and pulse testing are described. Finally a compilation of the most important expansions planned for the next future is given.

articleTitle: Characterization of a CISPR/VDE Far-Field EMI Test Site with Ground Screen
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The complex problem of measuring radiated EMI in the far-field is further complicated when measuring in close proximity to the earth. Because of reflections from the earth's surface, measured radiation from the system under test is a combination of both direct and reflected electromagnetic waves. Furthermore, the reflection coefficients depend upon the conductivity, permittivity and permeability of the earth and frequency. Thus, because of variations in these parameters, measurement results may not always be repeatable. However, if the earth is covered with a highly conductive material then soil variations can be expected to have little or no effect. In fact, the reflection coefficients at such a test site can be expected to closely approximate those values associated with a perfect conductor; that is, ε<sup>j0</sup> = 1 for vertically polarized incident waves, and ε<sup>J Π</sup> = 1 for horizontally-polarized incident waves.

articleTitle: Frequency Phase Analyzer of Low-Frequency Wideband Processes
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The structure diagram of frequency phase analyzer for investigation of wideband oscillation (0.1+100Hz) is discussed. The basic diagram element is a wideband Hilberter transformer. The maximum incorectness of frequency determination of short quasiharmonic switching can be 0.5%. The analyzer can be used in medical biological investigations for evaluation of influence of outer factors as well as of electromagnetic origin.

articleTitle: Some Characteristics of Electric Discharge as A Noise Source in EMC Problems — Recent Studies in Japan
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Noise due to electric discharge is investigated from BMC point of view. The general properties and the mechanisms of noise due to gap discharge and arc discharge in electric contacts are considered in experimental and partially in theoretical. This paper describes seme results obtained in Japan from fundamental studies.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Resulting from a Lightning Discharge, Surges Induced on Overhead Lines, Mathematical Model
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper presents the measurements of the electromagnetic field resulting from a lightning discharge. They were realized at distances ranging from 100 meters to 50 kilometers from the point of impact using large bandwith sensors. Recordings were made simultaneously on overhead lines, permitting an experimental link of the electromagnetic field to the surges induced on the lines. This paper also gives a description of a mathematical model we realized to relate the lightning current, the electromagnetic field and the surge induced on the line.

articleTitle: Power Distribution in a Prolate Spheroidal Model of Human Head Irradiated by Electromagnetic Plane Wave
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The prolate spheroid models are used to simulate human adult and infant heads. The internal electric field to first-order approximation has been obtained using the perturbation technique applied on Maxwell's equations. The specific time-averaged absorbed power and the space-averaged specific absorbed power are obtained from the internal electric field. It is shown that the power absorption depends on the head dielectric properties and geometry, as well as the frequency of radiation and polarization of the incident electromagnetic plane wave.

articleTitle: EMP Simulation and its impact on EMP Testing
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: In testing systems for their response to EMP it is necessary to consider the EMP criteria set. Then, having chosen some EMP simulation set, one must consider how closely each simulation approximates the respective criterion, correcting for this difference by extrapolation as necessary. This paper discusses these concepts in the context of currently used techniques.

articleTitle: Numerical Electromagnetics Code - A Program for Antenna System Analysis
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: A computer program entitled Numerical Electromagnetics Code(NEC) will be described and its various capabilities listed. An example of its applications to EMC analysis is presented. Also, its extensive documentation is described.

articleTitle: Lightning Induced Overvoltages in Buildings and Installed Equipment and Recommendations for Optimum Protection
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper deals with the overvoltage risks to extensive electronic systems in buildings due to voltage differences between the various parts of a structure's earth system (reinforcing steel, etc.). If it has not, so far, been possible to achieve optimum coordination between structural measures and requirements for overvoltage resistance of electronic equipment to be installed in a building, this is because data have not been available on either the voltages likely to occur in the event of lightning, or the quantitative influence of specific structural measures. The Swiss PTT R+D Division has now devised a method of measurement enabling both the voltage drop inside a building and the effect of exterior metal facing to be determined. This method, based on extensive model experiments, has been tried out at a newly erected PTT multipurpose building. The collected data enabled appropriate structural measures and requirements for overvoltage resistance of electronic equipment to be worked out and coordinated for optimum effect. The investigations, results and recommendations are contained in a PTT research paper [l], which serves as a basis for the specification of relevant structural, installation and equipment requirements.

articleTitle: Summation of Randomly Changing Vectors of Higher Harmonics with Special Regard to the Design of Network Filters for Metallurgical Drives
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Thyristor converters are used at present in the metallurgical drives in a still higher degree. However, they have besides many advantages also negative features occuring mainly in a poor power factor and the distortion of supply voltage /generating of higher harmonic currents into the supply network/. One way to a limitation of these reverse effects is the installation of network filters. The knowledge of the frequency spectrum of the thyristor converter current and its changes in the technological process is the fundamental assumption for an optimal design of these filters. The character of mechanical load of the metallurgical drives/so as of their currents/is highly fluctuating, so that there is no possibility of calculation with determined fixed quantities but only with their statistical characteristics, This paper contains the way to the experimental determination of higher harmonics distribution in the loads of metallurgical drives and the following simulation on a computer, in order to get analytical relations for the summation of these randomly changing currents. The results obtained by simulating on a computer were confirmed by the investigation of higher harmonics distribution in the summing supply points of the metallurgical rolling trains.

articleTitle: Impulse Wave Attenuation Factor of Shielding Cages
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The present work show the attenuation factor of an imperfect faraday cage with respect to stiff front time impulse waves. The of this work is to simulate the comportment of sensitive measuring electronic devices boxes against impulse phenomena. For testing the cage perfomances high precision data acquisition and processing is needed. An Original method permitting such measurements in a highly electromagneticaly perturbed environment is described. Result of measurements on a real scale for both the magnetic and electric field attenuation factor are given.

articleTitle: EMP Environments from Surface and High-Altitude Nuclear Explosions
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: In a previous paper<sup>1</sup>, this author briefly reviewed the theory of the electromagnetic pulse (EMP) produced by nuclear explosions. The present paper will be devoted to describing typical EMP environments resulting from nuclear bursts at very high altitudes and at low altitudes within a few hundred meters from the ground. These two cases appear to comprise the most important ones for practical concerns about EMP effects on electrical and electronic systems. The results presented are obtained from calculations, but the general validity of the calculations rests on experimental data as well.

articleTitle: The Detection and Identification of Bursts on Digital Highways
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper develops a theoretical approach aimed at identifying certain forms of result obtained by voltage threshold crossing detectors measuring common-mode interference on twisted pair data highways.

articleTitle: Matrix Iteration in Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Matrix iterative schemes are presented which save computer core storage or computing time in method of moments treatment of electromagnetic scattering problems. It is demonstrated that these savings can be considerable and could allow large or detailed objects to be treated. The convergence of the schemes is considered and a method of accelerating convergence discussed and applied. Some examples are presented.

articleTitle: The United Kingdom EMP Programme
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Although the UK had experienced EMP effects in nuclear tests it was not until the sixties that the civil and military authorities in general became activiely aware of the potentially hazardous effects of NEMP on their systems. The main areas of concern originally addressed were Army tactical support systems, aircraft, ships and static communication installations. Due to its nuclear weapon testing experience the Atomic Weapons Research Establishment (AWRE) has always been the main centre in the UK for R&D into EMP generation and effects and much of the work on simulator design, instrumentation and system assessment has been carried out there. Aircraft testing and assessment is performed at the Royal Aircraft Establishment (RAE) and the Aeroplane and Armament Experimental Establishment (A & AEE). The Admiralty Surface Weapons Establishment (ASWE) deals with ship-borne equipment. AWRE concerned themselves primarily with military systems and providing advice and support to defence contractors.

articleTitle: Propagation of Interference Currents on Power Mains
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The results of an empirical investigation of the propagation of interference currents over a variety of mains paths are presented. The length and complexity of the mains paths ranged from adjacent receptacles in the same outlet to adjacent single-family houses. Insertion loss curves for both common mode (asymmetric) and differential mode (symmetric) propagation in the frequency range of 500 kHz to 32 MHz are given. Curves of common mode-to-differential mode and differential mode-to-common mode conversions are also presented.

articleTitle: Measurement of Magnetic-Field and Electric-Field Emissions from Digital Radio Relays
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The measurement of spurious magnetic-field and electric-field emissions from digital radio relays in the vicinity of the apparatus have been undertaken by the CNET. Three principal kinds of radiated fields in the band between 10 kHz and 1 GHz have been determined and the level is on the order of 1 mV/m. The measurement procedure is close to the one specified by the MIL-462 American standard. Procedures specified by the CISPR are also used. Specific procedures are still utilized.

articleTitle: Methods to Assess the Hazard of EM Radiation to Ordnance
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The problem of assessing the Hazard of Electro magnetic Radiation to military systems which in corporate electro-explosive devices is becoming more and more important. The paper indicates a possible way to determine the level of safety that a weapon system can guarantee. This approach hinges on two keypoints: - the development of suitable instrumentation to detect the pick up of spurious energy induced into the EED's - the availability of a suitable test range to conduct those tests which simulate the environmental conditions in the most realistic manner. The paper describes some techniques and test facilities which are currently in use to clear weapon systems in Italy.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Influence on Biological Material
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The experimental evidence is presented on the influence of the constant, pulsed and the time varying magnetic fields on the biological material: The frog and mouse heart, the Retzius nerve cell and the human bone.

articleTitle: Ignition Noise of Foreign and Domestic Vehicles in Use in the United States
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Electromagnetic noise from the ignition systems of more than 11,000 individual vehicles in service in the United States in mid-1977 was measured at 50 and 153 MHz. We found very little difference between the noise of U.S. domestic and foreign vehicles. Older vehicle groups are noisier than newer vehicle-groups—a fact which may be accounted for by either of two causes: a) some vehicles in a group become noisier with age, b) newer vehicles may have improved noise suppression systems. Measurements made in a single year will not show which effect predominates. We found the greatest noise differences between vehicle types (cars, trucks, and so on).

articleTitle: EMP Studies on Underground Installations
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: An underground communications building was illuminated with a simulated EMP of low intensity. The penetration of the electromagnetic field into the ground was measured, and the screening effect of the rebar structure of the building was determined. Induced currents on cables inside and outside the building were measured. The experiment did not interfere with the normal operation of the installation.

articleTitle: A Method to Determine the MTBE of a Computer Subjected to Voltage Dips
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Considering the dips distribution on the mains (joint distribution magnitude/duration and occurrence of dips versus time), a model has been developed to generate, by means of a microcomputer, a string of dips occurring, in frequency, magnitude and duration, according to the desired distributions. The computer can drive a dip generator, simulating the disturbed main. So, after having defined the "standard disturbed main", it is possible to verify experimentally the MTBE (mean time between error) of the victim computer subjected to the dips. It is also possible, knowing the MTBE of the single subsystems, to predict the MTBE of the complete system. A suitable "immunity" function has been defined, so that the designer, on the basis of the target MTBE, is able to choose the cheapest solution. The method can be applied not only to the computers, but also to other equipments composed of a logic circuit driving electromechanical devices.

articleTitle: The CCIR and the World Administrative Radio Conference 1979
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Perhaps the most significant and most publicized event of the decade concerning the "electromagnetic compatibility" field will be the ITU World Administrative Radio Conference to be held in Genva for 10 weeks, from 24 September 1979.

articleTitle: The Measurement of Interference on Digital Highways: The Concept and Some Results
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper describes the concepts behind a programme of measurements of interference in the common-mode on balanced digital highways. The aims of the programme are to define the interference environment, and to predict the likely effects on future systems. The design of two instruments, which have been used to carry out the programme, is outlined. Preliminary results from the measurements are reported, and some analysis attempted of the small number of results so far.

articleTitle: Modelling of Aircraft Responses to EMP
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Surface current distributions on aircraft structures exposed to a plane electromagnetic wave have been calculated by means of an AWRE wire-grid modelling code 'CHAOS 3'. This uses the Method of Moments, overlapping triangular basis functions and a Galerkin type solution of the Electric Field Integral Equation. A number of (wire) junction routines are included. The program is capable of inverting large dense matrices and some 750 wire segments or more may be used. Modelling in considerable detail is therefore possible. Initial calculations are in frequency-domain with ready conversion to time-domain depending on the particular excitation being considered.

articleTitle: Test Method to Differentiate Common Mode and Differential Mode Noise
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: A new test method is described which separates common (asymmetrical) and differential (symmetrical) mode noise and yields quantitative data about each mode from 100 kHz to 20 MHz. The essential feature of this method is a modified r-f current probe combined with a high pass filter. The purpose of the high pass filter is to enhance the rejection of the power frequency current in the output of the current transformer.

articleTitle: A "TEM" Horn with Continuously Tapered Resistive Loading for Picoseond Pulse Measurements
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: For directional reception or transmission of picosecond pulses with minimal distortion, a short TEM horn with resistive loading was developed, and found to be broadband and nondispersive. Theoretical computations with the moment method and FFT were compared with time domain measurements.

articleTitle: Measurements of the over all City Noise
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Radio frequency noise radiated from a city is one measure of the electromagnetic enviroment. The noise may be caused by automobile ignition, power transmmission lines, electric switches, discharge tubes, manufacturai machines and others. From the stand point of surveillance, it must be measured the rf noise in the over all sense. The over all noise is supposed to have better correlations to human activities. We measured this kind of noise by using a system located on the top of the hill near the city. This measurement system has a high gain and sharp beam antenna, low noise amplifiers and an electric field intensity meater. This report presents some results obtained by this system. By rotating the sharp beam antenna, the distribution pattern of the noise sources were obtained. This system can measure the statistical parameters of the noise received by this system. Up to now, three typical APD curves were obtained.

articleTitle: Reduction of Electromagnetic Disturbances in Buildings Caused by Lightning using Conductive Facades
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Despite a complete meshed network of a lightning protection system, a significantly unequal current distribution in the individual down conductors occurs at unfavourable striking points in a building. When this happens especially the down conductors nearest the building facade conduct the greatest currents. Using conductive connections within the metalic facade elements, additional ways for the striking current can be created as discussed in this paper. The maximum current in the down conductors has been reduced on the fourth floor by about 1/3.

articleTitle: The Use of Computerized Analytical Techniques in Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The problem of efficiently managing the spectrum is becoming one of the main tasks of modern telecommunications. Techniques that automate data sorting and analyses are becoming increasingly necessary to efficiently accomplish the spectrum management process.

articleTitle: Application of the Nonlinear Circuit Analysis Program Ncap to Predict RFI Effects in Linear Bipolar Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Applications of the computer program NCAP to calculate RFI effects in electronic circuits containing discrete semiconductor devices have been reported upon previously. The objective of this paper is to demonstrate for the first time that the computer program NCAP can also be used to calculate RFI effects in linear bipolar integrated circuits (ICs). The IC reported upon is a differential pair which is a basic building block in many linear ICs. The differential pair was used as the active component in a broadband cascode amplifier circuit. The RFI effects predicted by NCAP and the experimental results measured in our laboratory are presented and compared. The comparison shows that the computer program NCAP predicts within ±5 dB how RF signals in the frequency range 0.1 to 100 MHz are demodulated in linear bipolar ICs to cause undesired low frequency responses.

articleTitle: A Modified Ebers-Moll Transistor Model for RF Interference Analysis
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper develops analytical techniques for the study of nonlinear RF and microwave effects in semiconductor devices. Rectification in PN junctions is discussed, and a novel large signal transistor model is developed based upon modifications to standard Ebers-Moll formulations for bipolar transistors.

articleTitle: Influences of Electromagnetic Fields in the Low-, Medium- and High Frequency Range on Biological Components
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: Electric and magnetic fields of high frequency with amplitudes up to 500 kV/m respectively 5000 A/m were generated in the object space of a microscope. Studies of the influence of these fields on bacteria, vegetable cells, animal cells and other biological objects showed nonthermal reactions which were microscopically visible only on electric fields. The amplitude and frequency responses of those phenomena were investigated systematically and led to remarkable similar characteristics of different types of reactions in different biological areas.

articleTitle: Swedish EMP Research
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The electromagnetic pulse, EMP or NEMP, from nuclear explosions has been studied since 1965 at FOA (the Swedish National Defence Research Institute). This paper reviews some of the last few years' research at FOA on the EMP phenomenology, coupling, effects, simulation, measurements, and protection.

articleTitle: A Nemp, Lightning and Power Line Induced Surge Protection Network of Low Capacitance for Transmission Equipment
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper presents a protection method for NEMP, lightning and power line induced surges, applicable to digital transmission equipment operating at transmission rates up to 2.048 Mbit/sec and over balanced lines. An arrangement of gas arrestors, metal oxyde varistors, silicon avalanche devices and limiting resistors is studied. Design considerations and laboratory test data are given.

articleTitle: A Simulator to Assess the Effects on Radio and TV Receivers of Interference Caused by Car Ignition Systems
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: A description of a car ignition system simulator to produce an interference voltage of very low value is given. A capacitive divider is the most peculiar part of this simulator, which can he used as a voltage noise source to be aja plied at the input terminals of a receiver together with the wanted signal in order to assess the effects of this kind of interference on radio and television reception. Some experimental results are reported.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Reduction of Volume of Measurements When Checking the Sources of Clicks for Compliance with CISPR Limits
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The present paper investigates probability distributions of click voltages which correspond to an upper quartale, and shows a possibility of use of non-central t-distribution for assessment of a batch of electrical appliances that are sources of clicks. Further it presents the results of investigations of possibilities of reducing the volume of measurements when checking the clicks by voltage magnitudes which correspond to an upper quartile.

articleTitle: Computer-Aided Analysis of RFI Effects in Operational Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: A computer-aided analysis procedure in conjunction with a modified Ebers-Moll transistor model is used to predict RFI effects in the 741 operational amplifier (op amp)—a bipolar linear integrated circuit (IC). RFI susceptibility predictions for RF incident upon the op amp input terminals are made using an op amp macromodel. The interactive program ISPICE is used to analyze the macromodel. The calculated results agree within 4 DB with experimental results measured at 220 MHz.

articleTitle: Numerical Method of Near-Field Evaluation, in Electromagnetic Interference Problems in Presence of the Earth
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: In many applications in the field of electromagnetic compatibility, the frequency-domain and transient responses of linear antennas over lossy ground must be investigated. The basic difficulty observed in incorporating the ground effects is the accurate evaluation of Sommerfeld-type integrals encountered when analyzing the electromagnetic field components. Analytical and approximate evaluation of these integrals are not available for all ranges of operating conditions, particulary in the proximal region of the electromagnetic sources. In this paper we present a fast numerical method for Sommerfeld integrals calculation with a given accuracy. This method is valid for the full range of interesting parameters. The accuracy of calculation is guaranteed providing that: - The variable range on the real axis, close to the branch-point appearing in the complex integrants is isolated. - An algorithm for Gauss-Romberg integration together with an original method using a self-adaptable interval subdivision is used. The rapidity of the numerical method is ensured by using a polynomial approximation of Bessel function appearing in Sommerfeld integral expressions, and an increased convergence method.

articleTitle: Susceptibility of Television Receivers and HI-FI Tuners to Signals in the Ghz-Range
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper describes investigations on susceptibilities of television receivers and Hi-Fi-tuners to signals in the GHz-range. Eight different television receivers and fifteen Hi-Fi-tuners, representing different manufacturers, have been tested. Tests have been conducted with an amplitude modulated interfering signal at 2450 ± 50 MHz, 3150 ± 50 MHz, 5800 ± 75 MHz and at 24125 ± 125 MHz. As susceptibility threshold criterion at TV-receivers the screen was observed if any visible interference pattern occured, according to IEC-Publ. 107. At Hi-Fi-tuners the decrease of S/N ratio was taken as criterion, according to DIN 45500. All tested equipment has shown a maximum of susceptibility at 2450 MHz. The interference threshold level for TV-receivers was approxmiately ≥ 2.5 V/m and for Hi-Fi-tuners approxmiately ≥ 3 V/m respectively. At higher frequencies the tested equipment has shown decreasing susceptibilities.

articleTitle: Computation and Presentation of Electromagnetic Fields for Variousconductive Structures on the Incidence of Steep Pulses
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: For various metallic structures the time dependent electromagnetic field distributions after incidence of an EMP were calculated. Field lines were drawn in order to present the development of the steady state in a slow motion animated film. While the surface current distribution and the electric field outside the conductor is established within nanoseconds it takes microseconds for the magnetic field to penetrate through conductive walls. Intention of this presentation is to give some insight into the interaction between non-sinusoidal fields and conductive obstacles.

articleTitle: The Evolution of EMC Techniques for the Control of the Low-Frequency Magnetic Environment
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: The case is introduced for an extension of routine EMC testing of equipment to frequencies below 10kHz, based on Royal Navy experience and on certain equipment design trends which call for tighter control of the low-frequency magnetic environment if electromagnetic compatibility is to be achieved. Some standard results from the theory of magnetostatics are presented, including the definition of a magnetic dipole moment and general formulae for the fields surrounding a current loop. These results are used to discuss field measurements at the surface of an equipment enclosure and their relation to internal dipole moments. The concept of magnetic moment per unit volume is introduced, and formulae are presented which relate this quantity to the maximum normal component of the B field at any point on the surface of enclosures of various shapes. A ‘magnetic emission’ test method is described, based on the MIL-STD-462 RE01 test loop used in conjunction with a modern digital spectrum analyser. The choice of a suitable magnetic emission specification level is discussed on the basis of results obtained from applying this test to a wide variety of naval equipments. The choice adopted is shown to be consistent with the results of magnetic environmental surveys conducted in typical modern warships, and amounts to an increase in the existing RE01 limits by 30dB. It is concluded that the adoption of this specification level will allow all but a minority of equipments to be designed to comply at no significant increase in cost, weight, or space. The few exceptions will be specifically identified and subjected to constraints in their permitted siting relative to highly-susceptible equipments. The requirements for a complementary magnetic susceptibility test method and specification are mentioned but not discussed.

articleTitle: Computational Techniques for EMP Interaction
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: This paper discusses some of the recent developments pertaining to computational techniques for EMP interaction. A survey of various computational methods is presented and a number of comparisons of experimental and computed data are given for various aircraft.

articleTitle: Near Field Antenna Coupling Theory in a Shielded Room: The Mutual Impedance Model
publicationTitle: 3rd Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Rotterdam
abstract: A theoretical model is developed which predicts the coupling between two closely spaced antennas in the presence of a reflector. Measured results are presented which prove the validity of the model, and it is shown how the model will be extended to fully describe the coupling between two antennas in a shielded room.

articleTitle: Research on Artificially Triggered Lightning in France
